headline: Strong cold front brings damaging wind, heavy rain and dangerous surf tonight into Sunday; more wet systems follow next week.
summary: A strong cold front crosses western Washington from this evening into early Sunday morning, bringing widespread lowland rain, gusty south winds, mountain snow at higher elevations and very high surf on the coast. Wind is the main concern. Forecasters give a 50-70% chance of gusts over 55 mph along the coast, where a High Wind Warning is in effect from 4 PM Saturday to 4 AM Sunday. Interior lowlands, including Seattle, are under a Wind Advisory from 6 PM Saturday to 4 AM Sunday for gusts of 45 to 50 mph at times. Many trees still have leaves, so localized power outages are possible. Heavy rain at the same time as the wind could clog storm drains this evening, so allow extra travel time. Winds peak overnight into early Sunday morning and ease steadily through late Sunday afternoon. Waves of 22 to 28 feet are expected on the beaches tonight, with a High Surf Warning from 10 PM Saturday to 10 PM Sunday. Big waves and strong wind make the razor clam dig dangerous. There is a 20-30% chance of isolated thunderstorms, mainly on the coast, and a 10-20% chance in the interior, where a lightning strike or two is possible. On Sunday the steady rain turns to showers, mostly over the North Cascades and Olympics. The snow level (the elevation where rain turns to snow) drops from around 7000-7500 feet to 4500 feet, bringing some snow to higher mountain terrain. Highs are in the mid 50s. After a break Sunday evening, another system arrives Monday with widespread rain and locally breezy conditions, again with the most rain over the Olympics. Wet, breezy weather continues Tuesday into Wednesday with warmer temperatures, and more systems are expected late in the week. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will saturate soils and raise river flows, which could become a concern if storms arrive late next week. Forecasters are fairly confident in tonight's wind and rain. They call computer model guidance for next week "a bit shaky" on the timing and strength of the systems, though an active pattern looks likely.
changes: The wind and surf forecast held steady through the day: the 9 AM update moved from a watch to the High Wind Warning and added Wind Advisories, and the afternoon update raised the top wave height from 26 to 28 feet. The afternoon update also added thunderstorm chances, the storm-drain concern and snow level details, and dropped the earlier mention of near-record warmth Wednesday, saying only that next week's timing is less certain.
